o: Classify five cards: Flush if all suits equal; otherwise Three of a Kind if some rank appears ≥3 times; Pair if some rank appears exactly 2+ times; else High Card. Note a hand can satisfy multiple categories (e.g., example 2 is also a pair) — return the best. Constraints (5 cards, ranks 1..13, suits a..d, no duplicate rank+suit) make this a direct counting exercise.
k: Flush check: all five suits identical — checked first since it outranks rank-based hands.
Rank frequency max determines Three of a Kind (≥3) vs Pair (≥2) vs High Card.
Order of checks encodes the ranking; no complex logic needed.

a.i: Count suits (set size 1 ⇒ Flush) and rank multiplicities (max count decides among the remaining categories).
s: Count rank frequencies; let m = max count.
Return "Three of a Kind" if m ≥ 3, "Pair" if m = 2, else "High Card".

w: Trivial problem; the only care points are exact output strings (case-sensitive) and checking Flush before rank-based hands. Follow-up: extend to full poker rankings (straight, full house) — still just counting plus a sorted-rank run check.
